findings.name: Palisades Tahoe parking - 2026-27 paid reservation (THE CLEAREST CONFIRMED PARKING FEE)
findings.claim: Palisades Tahoe's own parking-program page is already updated for the 2026-27 season and states the fee outright: '$30 per car, per day on Saturdays, Sundays, and select holidays periods'. Reservations are required on Saturdays, Sundays and select holiday periods across the whole listed calendar: December 5th-6th, 12th-13th, 19th-31st; January 1st-3rd, 9th-10th, 16th-18th, 23rd-24th, 30th-31st; February 6th-7th, 13th-21st, 27th-28th; March 6th-7th, 13th-14th, 20th-21st, 27th-28th; April 3rd-4th and 10th-11th. Critically, the $30 is the OPTIONAL advance-purchase price: 'Free parking reservations for the coming weekend will be released each week' on Tuesdays at 12:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. Pacific, with 50% released at each drop. So $30/car/day is the price of certainty, not the price of parking. The carpool incentive is real money back: 'Carpool 4+ drivers will receive a $20 resort credit voucher.' For a party of 6 this is the sawtooth again - 6 people in ONE vehicle qualifies for the carpool voucher; 6 people split across TWO cars means 3 per car and NEITHER car qualifies. All midweek (Mon-Fri) parking is free with no reservation. Trailers, campers and towed vehicles are banned from the lots entirely.
findings.price_usd: $30 per car per day (advance paid reservation); $0 for a free reservation released weekly; $0 midweek
findings.restrictions: Only applies Sat/Sun and the listed holiday periods, Dec 5 2026 - Apr 11 2027. Free reservations are released weekly on Tuesdays and sell out. Carpool of 4+ occupants gets a free reservation plus a $20 resort credit. No trailers/campers.

State Parks confirms 'Permits for the 2026/2027 SNO-Park Permit Season will be available approximately October 2026', so the $15/$40 figures are the currently published rates carried into the 26/27 season, not yet a 26/27 price list.

findings.name: The site's $90/car gas assumption is TOO LOW - it only works for a hybrid
findings.claim: DERIVED, not quoted - every input is sourced but the total is arithmetic, so treat it as an estimate. San Jose to Truckee is approximately 218 driving miles each way (secondary sources: travelmath/trippy; I could not fetch a primary mapping source), so ~436 miles round trip. Add the in-area driving a 4-ski-day trip actually generates - Truckee to Donner Summit and back is roughly 15-25 miles each way, so call it 80-120 miles - and the trip is ~520-560 miles. At the confirmed San Jose price of $5.5840/gal: a 30-mpg sedan burns ~18 gal = ~$100; a 22-mpg midsize SUV burns ~24.5 gal = ~$137; an 18-mpg full-size AWD SUV (a Suburban/Tahoe, which is what you rent when six people plus skis need one vehicle) burns ~30 gal = ~$167. A 45-mpg hybrid comes in around $67. The site's flat GAS_PER_CAR = 90 in lib/quote.ts is therefore roughly right ONLY for a small efficient car and understates a realistic SUV by $45-80 per car. Recommend making it mpg-dependent, or at minimum raising the SUV case. Note also that this assumes you refuel at Bay Area prices; Sierra-corridor stations are dearer (see the negative finding on Truckee gas).
findings.price_usd: ~$100 sedan / ~$137 midsize SUV / ~$167 full-size AWD SUV round trip incl. local driving
findings.restrictions: Arithmetic from a confirmed $5.5840/gal and an approximate 218-mile one-way distance. Distance is from secondary mapping sites, not a primary source. Winter fuel economy runs 10-20% worse than rated in cold weather and with a roof box, so these are optimistic.
findings.season_confirmed: Built on a 2026-08-27 gas price, not a winter 2026-27 price

verification.why: I tried to break this one and could not. The code claim is real: lib/quote.ts line 35 is 'const GAS_PER_CAR = 90;' and it is applied per car at lines 76-77. The gas input is CONFIRMED at $5.5840/gal. findings.name: Caltrans chain controls - R1/R2/R3 in the state's own words, and the AWD trap
findings.claim: Caltrans' official definitions: R-1 is 'Chains are required on all vehicles except passenger vehicles and light-duty trucks under 6,000 pounds gross weight and equipped with snow tires on at least two drive wheels.' R-2 is 'Chains or traction devices are required on all vehicles except four-wheel/all-wheel drive vehicles with snow-tread tires on all four wheels.' R-3 is 'Chains or traction devices are required on all vehicles, no exceptions.' Two lines matter enormously for this trip and the site says nothing about either. First: 'Four-wheel/all-wheel drive vehicles must carry traction devices in chain control areas' - AWD does not exempt you from CARRYING chains, only from fitting them under R-2. Second, R-2 exempts AWD only with snow-tread tires on all four wheels; the all-season tires on a rental Highlander are not snow-tread, so an AWD rental can legally be turned around at an R-2 check. Caltrans also states 'Chain installers are NOT allowed to sell or rent chains', which means if you arrive at a control without chains, the roadside installer cannot sell you a set - you must have bought them below the snow line.
findings.restrictions: R-1 and R-2 are the common conditions on I-80; the road is usually closed before R-3 is imposed. Chains must be carried in the control area even by AWD vehicles. Installers cannot sell or rent chains to you.
findings.season_confirmed: Standing Caltrans regulation, not season-specific; page live as of 2026-08-27

findings.name: Les Schwab's free spring refund on unused chains - effectively makes chains a $0 rental
findings.claim: The single best cost hack I found for this whole dimension, quoted from Les Schwab's own page: 'if your quick-fit chains, tire socks, or other traction devices remain unused at the end of the season, bring them back to any Les Schwab for a full refund in the spring.' Their warranty section heads this 'Full Refund for Unused Passenger or Light Truck Tire Chains' and conditions it on proper storage and no rust. They also say staff 'can show you how to install them with a quick, in-store lesson.' Practical effect: buy chains at a Bay Area Les Schwab before leaving, and if you never fit them - which is the likely outcome on a flexible-dates trip - the chains cost $0. The catch for the site's model is that Les Schwab publishes NO prices online at all; you have to walk in or call. So the refund policy is confirmed, the price is not.
findings.restrictions: Refund requires the chains to be genuinely unused, properly stored and not rusted, returned in the spring. Applies to passenger/light-truck chains. Les Schwab does not publish chain prices online.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE / UNVERIFIED. Search results point to an NBC Bay Area report that licensed installers on I-80 and Highway 50 raised their fee 'from $30 to $40', with $30-50 quoted as the working range elsewhere and removal typically costing extra. The NBC article returns HTTP 403 to fetch and the Caltrans District chain-installer page 404s, so I have NO primary confirmation of any installer fee and no evidence Caltrans caps it. What IS confirmed from Caltrans: installers are permitted by the state, and they 'are NOT allowed to sell or rent chains'. Treat any installer fee on the site as an unsourced estimate or omit it - the honest framing is 'installers work the chain-up areas westbound at Truckee Scales (Exit 186) and Nyack (Exit 174) for a cash fee; budget something, we could not confirm what'.
findings.restrictions: Installers are cash-oriented, cannot sell you chains, and typically charge separately for removal. You can always fit chains yourself for free in the designated chain-up areas.
findings.season_confirmed: NONE - no primary source obtained

findings.name: Enterprise forbids snow chains on its rental cars - the biggest hidden risk in the $500/car plan
findings.claim: This is the finding that should change the site's rental-car page. Enterprise's own FAQ (surfaced in search; the page itself returns HTTP 403 to fetch, so I flag it as unconfirmed-at-source) states that Enterprise does not offer snow chains or traction devices, nor can snow chains/traction devices be placed on rental vehicles unless required by state law, with a named exception for Colorado Code 15/16 advisories. Read that against the confirmed Caltrans rules above: under R-1 a 2WD rental sedan on all-season tires legally REQUIRES chains, and under R-2 it requires them absolutely. If the rental contract forbids fitting chains, a 2WD rental has no lawful way through an active chain control - you turn around. The workaround the industry actually uses is that California chain-control law is 'required by state law', which arguably triggers Enterprise's own exception, but that is a reading, not a quoted policy. ACTION for the site: if the group rents, rent AWD/4WD with genuinely snow-rated tires, or accept that a storm day may cost them the drive entirely. Confirm the chain clause with the specific branch before booking.
findings.restrictions: Policy as surfaced: no chains provided, none may be fitted unless state law requires it. Enterprise's page could not be fetched directly to confirm the exact current wording.
findings.season_confirmed: Standing policy, no season stated; not confirmed at source

findings.name: Under-25 surcharges - the line item the site's flat $500/car completely omits
findings.claim: UNVERIFIED AT SOURCE but consistent across every secondary source, and material enough that the site must at least caption it. Turo: young-driver fees of $50/day for ages 18-20 and $30/day for ages 21-24, applied to every listed driver under 25 on the trip, not just the booker. Over a 5-night trip that is $150-$250 PER under-25 driver, on top of the car. Enterprise: minimum age 21 in California, Young Renter Fee around $25/day for ages 21-24 - roughly $125 over the trip - and, crucially, a vehicle-class restriction: 21-24 renters are limited to economy through full-size cars, minivans, pickups and 'Compact SUVs, Small SUVs and Standard SUVs with seating up to 5 passengers'. That last clause is the killer for a group of 6: a 21-24 year old renter may not be able to rent the large SUV the group actually needs. Hertz is worse - reports say full-size SUVs are restricted to 25+, with 21-24 limited to economy/compact/intermediate, at a surcharge around $13.50/day capped near $189. Turo's help pages truncate and Enterprise's returns 403, so none of these numbers are confirmed at source. But the shape of the finding - a per-day surcharge AND a vehicle-class ceiling - is unanimous.
findings.restrictions: Applies to every driver under 25 listed on the rental, not just one. Vehicle-class caps are the bigger problem: Enterprise caps 21-24 renters at standard SUVs seating 5; Hertz reportedly bars 21-24 from full-size SUVs entirely. A group of 6 needing one large SUV may need a 25+ driver on the contract.
findings.season_confirmed: Current policy as reported 2026; not confirmed at any primary page

verification.checked_by: skeptic pass (Turo help page x2, Turo policy page, Enterprise young-renters page)
verification.why: The QUALITATIVE finding survives; every dollar figure fails. Turo's own Driver eligibility help page truncates before any fee table on two separate fetches, and turo.com/us/en/policies/young-driver-fee returns HTTP 403. What IS confirmable from Turo's own help content is only the shape: guests must be 18+, drivers under 25 pay a young driver fee, and the fee 'can't be removed or refunded at the end of a trip'. No amount. Enterprise's young-renters FAQ returns HTTP 403, so neither the ~$25/day fee nor - more importantly - the vehicle-class ceiling that would stop a 21-24 renter from taking the large SUV a party of six needs could be confirmed. The $50/$30/$25/$13.50 figures trace only to secondary aggregator blogs. Nulled.
corrections: price_usd and per_day_usd nulled. The site may say 'renters under 25 pay a per-day surcharge and may be barred from large SUVs - confirm with the agency', but must print no number.
The vehicle-class restriction is the more expensive half of this finding for a group of 6 and is equally unconfirmed. Flag it as a question to ask the branch, not as a fact.

findings.name: San Jose SUV rental market rates - the $500/car flat assumption is roughly right, slightly optimistic
findings.claim: KAYAK's San Jose SUV rental page (an aggregator, so medium at best, but the figures are its own published market statistics rather than a snippet) states 'on average an SUV rental in San Jose costs $91 per day', with weekly rentals averaging '$638'. It names 'January is typically the cheapest month to rent an SUV in San Jose, with prices around $61 per day' against a July peak of $83 - so a flexible-dates group booking January is buying at the annual low. Class-level floors: standard and compact SUVs from '$40/day', a Chevrolet Suburban at '$126/day', an oversize SUV class at '$132/day'. Sanity check against lib/types.ts CAR_RENTAL_PER_TRIP = 500: a 5-day January SUV at $61/day is $305 base, but SJC airport pickup adds a $10 customer facility charge, San Jose sales tax of 9.38%, an energy recovery surcharge and an airport concession recovery fee I could not pin down - realistically 25-35% on top, landing around $400-$450. So $500 holds for a standard SUV booked in January. It does NOT hold for the Suburban-class vehicle a party of 6 with skis actually wants ($126/day x 5 = $630 base, ~$800+ all-in), and it does not include any under-25 surcharge. Recommend the site split the assumption by vehicle size.
findings.price_usd: $73/day San Jose SUV average (CORRECTED from $91); $61/day January average; $638/week ($91/day equivalent); Suburban $126/day; oversize SUV $132/day
findings.per_day_usd: $61-$132 per day depending on class and month
findings.restrictions: Aggregator market statistics, not a quote for specific dates. Excludes airport fees ($10 CFC + 9.38% San Jose sales tax + energy recovery surcharge + concession recovery fee), young-driver surcharges, and any ski-rack or AWD upcharge. Booking ~70 days out is cited as ~33% cheaper than last-minute.
findings.season_confirmed: Current market statistics as of 2026-08-27; January figure is a seasonal average, not a 2027 quote

verification.checked_by: skeptic pass (independent re-fetch of the cited page)
verification.season_on_live_page: live market statistics as of 2026-08-27; no season label
verification.why: MISQUOTE FOUND. The original attributes to KAYAK the sentence 'on average an SUV rental in San Jose costs $91 per day'. The live page says something different: 'On average, a SUV rental in San Jose costs $73 per day.' The $91 is real but it is a DIFFERENT statistic - it is the per-day equivalent embedded in the weekly figure, 'On average an SUV in San Jose costs $638 per week ($91 per day) to rent.' The original collapsed two stats into one and quoted the wrong one as the headline daily average, overstating it by 25%. The remaining figures all check out verbatim: '$61 per day' January, '$638' per week, '$126/day' Suburban, '$132/day' oversize SUV class. Confidence downgraded because a finding with a misquote in it should not sit at medium, and because these are aggregator market statistics, not a quote for the group's dates.
corrections: $91/day was NOT the SUV daily average. Corrected: the daily average is $73/day; $91/day is the implied rate inside the $638 weekly average.

The finding's actual conclusion is unaffected: at the confirmed $61/day January rate a 5-day standard SUV is $305 base and $500 all-in is defensible, while the confirmed $126/day Suburban is not covered by $500. That part stands.

findings.name: Ski racks and AWD from the majors - NO published price found anywhere
findings.claim: NEGATIVE RESULT. I could not find a published price for a ski rack or a guaranteed-AWD upgrade from Enterprise, Hertz or Turo at any primary source - Enterprise and Turo both return 403 to fetch and none of the aggregators price these as line items. What I can say from the sources that did load: the majors sell SUVs by CLASS, not by drivetrain, so 'AWD' is generally not a bookable guarantee at Enterprise/Hertz - you get what is on the lot. Turo, by contrast, lists individual vehicles so you can see the actual drivetrain and whether the host includes a rack, but hosts price extras individually with no platform-wide rate. Tahoe Donner's shuttle page notes their vehicles are 'equipped with ski and snowboard racks', which is a free alternative to carrying gear on a car. The site should not print a ski-rack price. If gear transport matters, the honest advice is that skis fit inside any SUV with a seat folded, and a party of 6 with 6 sets of skis needs the large SUV anyway.
findings.restrictions: AWD is generally not guaranteeable at the major agencies; it is selectable on Turo. No rack pricing published.
findings.season_confirmed: NONE

findings.name: The Hotel at Sugar Bowl (Village Lodge) - the only real hotel on Donner Summit, rates published
findings.claim: Sugar Bowl's own lodging page publishes a 'Winter Rates' table for its 27-room slopeside Village Lodge - the only conventional hotel actually on Donner Summit, reached by gondola from the parking area: Northern Twin 'Starting at $239', Mountain View '$269', Northern Loft '$319', Mountain Family and Mountain Deluxe '$339', Northern Family '$449', Family Connector '$489', Deluxe Suite '$719'. For 6 people you would need two rooms - two Mountain Family rooms is $678/night, i.e. $113/person/night before tax, which is expensive against the $60/day lift benchmark this whole trip is built around. Policies confirmed on the page: no lift tickets are included with lodging, no resort fee is mentioned, full advance deposit is required for all reservations, 'Check-in time is at 4:00 pm and check-out times is by 11:00 am', no refunds for late arrival or early departure, and non-refundable cancellation fees scale with timing. SEASON CAVEAT: the table is headed 'Winter Rates' with no year. The same site states 'Our targeted Opening Day is Friday, November 27, 2026', so the page is being maintained for 26/27, but the rates themselves are not year-labelled - and every figure is 'Starting at', meaning holiday-period pricing will be higher.
findings.per_day_usd: ~$113/person/night for 6 in two Mountain Family rooms, before tax
findings.restrictions: 'Starting at' prices - late Dec / early Jan will price above these. Lift tickets NOT included. Full advance deposit; no refund for early departure; tiered cancellation fees. Rooms sleep 2-4, so 6 people need 2 rooms.
findings.season_confirmed: NOT year-labelled on the page; the site elsewhere names 2026-27 opening day, so treat as current published winter rates, not confirmed 26/27

findings.name: Sugar Bowl ski-in/ski-out property rentals - $550/night for a 4BR is the best per-head number on the Summit
findings.claim: The same Sugar Bowl page lists whole-house rentals in the snowbound village at flat winter nightly rates that do not change between weekday and weekend: townhomes (4-bedroom) at '$550/night' for both Sunday-Wednesday and Thursday-Saturday, Summit Crossing #11 (4BR) at '$1,000/night', West Village #01 (5BR) at '$1,200/night', and East Village #35 (6BR) at '$1,000/night'. The $550 4-bedroom townhome is the standout: for a party of 6 that is $91.67 per person per night, and unlike the lodge rooms the rate is flat across the week. Over 5 nights that is $2,750 for the group, $458/person, ski-in/ski-out on Donner Summit with no parking fee and no drive to the hill. Same season caveat as the lodge rates - the table separates 'Winter' from 'Summer' pricing but names no year, and holiday minimums are not published on the page.
findings.per_day_usd: $91.67 per person per night for 6 in the $550 townhome
findings.restrictions: Winter rate quoted flat Sun-Wed and Thu-Sat, but no holiday-period rate or minimum-stay rule is published on the page - late Dec / early Jan almost certainly carries both. Full advance deposit; non-refundable cancellation fees.
findings.season_confirmed: 'Winter' pricing with no year stated; page live 2026-08-27 and maintained for the 2026-27 season

findings.name: Clair Tappaan Lodge - the classic Donner Summit budget option, but NO rate is published anywhere I could read
findings.claim: IMPORTANT NEGATIVE. Clair Tappaan Lodge (19940 Donner Pass Rd, Norden - walking distance to Sugar Bowl, minutes from Donner Ski Ranch and Boreal) is the obvious hostel-style answer for a price-sensitive group of 6, and it publishes NOTHING. Its own site has an accommodations page, a rustic-accommodations page and a sitemap with no rates page at all; the 'Book Now' control is a javascript:void(0) that opens a JS booking widget I cannot read. Secondary sources conflict badly and are clearly of different vintages: older write-ups say '$60 per adult including all meals, half that for kids 4-13'; OTA listings for 2026 dates show a room rate around $122-$142/night with the note that 'Breakfast, lunch and dinner are not included in the room rate, but can be added', with meals quoted around $57 per person. Those describe two completely different products, so I will not report either as the price. What IS confirmed: the Sierra Club still operates it, its cabins and bunk rooms became bookable on Hipcamp for the winter season as of January 2026, and the room inventory is single-gender bunk rooms (5-18 beds), two-person rooms, and private rooms suitable for groups of 5-12. The site should link to it, describe it as hostel-style with optional family-style meals, and state that a quote requires contacting the lodge (530-426-3632) - not print a number.
findings.restrictions: Bunk rooms are single-gender with communal bathrooms; blankets historically a small extra charge. Meals are served family-style at fixed times (dinner 6pm, breakfast 8am) and per OTA listings must be added at booking, not on arrival. Sierra Club members get a discount at check-in. Private rooms suit groups of 5-12.
findings.season_confirmed: NONE - no 2026-27 rate published on the lodge's own site or readable at any booking source

findings.name: Rainbow Lodge, Soda Springs - reopened, 15 rooms, but publishes no nightly rates
findings.claim: NEGATIVE RESULT. Rainbow Lodge (50080 Hampshire Rocks Rd, Soda Springs - the 1869 lodge on 114 acres along the South Yuba, just off I-80 below the summit) has reopened and is taking overnight bookings, but neither its site nor its reservations page shows a single nightly rate. The booking link goes to therainbowlodge.client.innroad.com, which is a bare InnRoad JavaScript shell with no server-rendered prices. The only dollar figures anywhere are WEDDING-package numbers from a venue directory (a $3,000 second-night add-on, '$150/night' for additional adult guest rooms, '$500 total' for four kids' rooms) - those are buyout/event pricing, NOT a normal nightly rate, and reporting them as room rates would be actively misleading. Confirmed non-price facts: 15 overnight guest rooms sleeping up to 40 guests including a first-floor suite, updated furnishings, restaurant and full bar on site, breakfast reported as complimentary, overnight capacity of 65 for events. Contact (530) 718-3009 / info@therainbowlodge.com for a quote. It is in unincorporated Nevada County, so the county's 10% TOT applies rather than Truckee's 14%.
findings.restrictions: 15 rooms total - a group of 6 would likely fit but the property also does full buyouts for events, so weekend availability in ski season may be blocked. No online rate display.
findings.season_confirmed: NONE

findings.name: Truckee chain hotels - the flexible-dates arbitrage is enormous
findings.claim: Aggregator market data (medium confidence - these are the booking sites' own published statistics, not quotes for specific dates). For Truckee Donner Lodge specifically, KAYAK shows a cheapest King room at '$110', Executive room 2 doubles at '$141', standard at '$147', and Executive/Queen 2-queen rooms swinging from '$149' up to '$390' depending on date; its monthly averages are '$121' in May against '$278' in December, with weeknights averaging '$179' and weekend nights '$226'. The property's Family Suite sleeps 6 (2 bedrooms, 2 queens plus a double sofa bed), so one suite can hold the whole group. Market-wide, momondo puts the Truckee average around '$421 per night' and names the extremes explicitly: 'February, with an average cost of $757/night' as the most expensive month, against 'April, with an average cost of $252/night' as the cheapest - a 3x spread. Named properties with prices: Truckee Donner Lodge $145, SpringHill Suites Truckee $146, Tahoe Star Hotel $275, West River House $97 as the market floor. THE HEADLINE FOR A DATE-FLEXIBLE GROUP: moving the trip off February and off the Christmas/New Year window into early December, mid-January or late March/April cuts the lodging line roughly in half. That is a bigger lever than anything on the lift-ticket side.
findings.price_usd: $110-$390/night Truckee Donner Lodge by date; Truckee market average ~$421/night; February ~$757/night vs April ~$252/night
findings.per_day_usd: ~$18-$47 per person per night for 6 in one Family Suite at $110-$278
findings.restrictions: Aggregator statistics, not quotes for specific 2026-27 dates. Late Dec / early Jan will price at or above the February peak. A 6-person Family Suite is a single room type with limited inventory - book early or split into two standard rooms.
findings.season_confirmed: Current market data as of 2026-08-27; monthly averages are historical seasonality, NOT confirmed 2026-27 rates

findings.name: Truckee lodging tax went UP on 1 July 2026 - 14% on every night, and on cleaning fees too
findings.claim: A confirmed, current, primary-source hidden fee the site ignores entirely. The Town of Truckee states its transient occupancy tax is 12% and its Tourism Business Improvement District assessment was 1.25% for a combined guest levy of 13.25% - but that 'Rates Effective July 1, 2026' the TTBID rises to 2%, taking the combined total guest levy to 14%. It applies to any 'stay of less than 31 continuous nights' and to hotels and short-term rentals alike, and the taxable base is broad: 'nightly rents, cleaning fees, pet fees, booking fees, and other mandatory charges'. So a $2,000 Truckee lodging subtotal is $2,280 out the door, and the cleaning fee gets taxed too. NOTE THE GEOGRAPHY ARBITRAGE: this is the TOWN of Truckee. Soda Springs, Norden and Donner Summit are unincorporated NEVADA COUNTY, where the county TOT is reported at 10% (I could not fetch the county page - it returns 403 - so treat the 10% as medium confidence). Staying on the Summit rather than in town is worth roughly 4 percentage points on top of being closer to the cheap lifts.
findings.price_usd: 14% of the lodging subtotal in the Town of Truckee (12% TOT + 2% TTBID), effective 2026-07-01
findings.restrictions: Applies to stays under 31 continuous nights, hotels and short-term rentals both. Taxable base includes cleaning fees, pet fees and booking fees, not just room rate. Unincorporated Nevada County (Soda Springs/Norden/Donner Summit) is reported at 10% instead - medium confidence, county page not fetchable.
findings.season_confirmed: Rate confirmed effective 2026-07-01, so it is the rate in force for the entire 2026-27 ski season

findings.name: Free shuttles that zero out the parking fees - but the 2026-27 dates are not out yet
findings.claim: PARTIAL NEGATIVE with a real planning payoff. Palisades Tahoe's Park and Ride is free and the page confirms the parking locations - '11611 Donner Pass Rd, Truckee, CA 96161' at the TTUSD lot, and '180 W Lake Blvd, Tahoe City' - with shuttles departing 'between 6:30 and 7:45 each morning' and returning 'until 5:45 p.m.'. But the page is explicitly labelled the '2025-26 season' and gives dates of December 27, 2025 through April 12, 2026, weekends only. The 2026-27 dates are NOT published as of 2026-08-27; the parking program page says to stay tuned for 2026-27 releases. Also free per the Truckee DMO: TART Connect on-demand micro-transit across Truckee and North Tahoe (Tahoe Donner's page says it runs 'throughout the winter from 6:30AM to 10PM' in 4WD vehicles with ski racks), the Sugar Bowl/Donner Summit shuttle, and Northstar's Castle Peak free lot with continuous free shuttle. Bottom line for the site: the $30 Palisades and $25 Sierra parking fees are avoidable at $0 by a group willing to park in Truckee and ride, or by putting all 6 people in one vehicle to trigger the carpool exemptions.
findings.restrictions: 2026-27 operating dates unpublished as of 2026-08-27; the 2025-26 program was weekends only, Dec 27 - Apr 12, with a fixed morning departure window. Palisades Park and Ride drops at the Village only, not Alpine.
findings.season_confirmed: 2025-26 ONLY - the 2026-27 shuttle calendar has not been released

findings.name: Diamond Peak parking - free general, $30/$35 preferred, but the page is a season stale
findings.claim: Diamond Peak (Incline Village, NV - the far side of the lake from Donner Summit, included only for completeness) states: 'Parking is free, but we do offer paid preferred slope-side parking for $30 weekends and $35 peak periods, while supplies last', with the reservation holding 'a spot for your standard-sized vehicle in our paid parking lot until 12pm'. The page is labelled 2025-26 and currently reads 'Closed for the 2025-26 season. See you in December!', so these are last season's numbers and 2026-27 pricing is unpublished. Reported here mainly as evidence of how widespread the paid-preferred-parking model has become across Tahoe - Palisades $30, Sugar Bowl $35, Diamond Peak $30-35, Sierra-at-Tahoe $25, Kirkwood $20 - and how consistently free parking still exists underneath it.
findings.price_usd: $30 weekends / $35 peak periods for preferred parking; $0 general parking
findings.restrictions: Preferred spot held only until 12pm, standard-sized vehicles, 'while supplies last'. General parking free.
findings.season_confirmed: 2025-26 - the page states it is closed for the 2025-26 season and has not been updated for 2026-27

findings.name: Donner Lake area small inns - a few real numbers, but tiny inventory
findings.claim: Two Donner-Lake-adjacent options that are neither Airbnb nor a chain. Donner Lake Inn B&B: trip.com shows an average price of 'USD214' per night with rooms 'starting at US$206', for Superior and Deluxe Studio Suites with multiple beds, refrigerator and microwave - but those figures are from an early-September date query, not a ski-season one, and the property is only FIVE rooms with a complimentary grab-and-go breakfast, so a group of 6 would need most of the inn. Donner Lake Village (15695 Donner Pass Rd, on the lake, ~4.6 miles from Sugar Bowl) rents studio, 1BR and 2BR condo units and states that winter rates run November 1 through April 30 split into non-Holiday and Holiday nightly rates - but its site requires dates to show any price ('Enter Dates For Pricing') and I could not get a rendered rate, so I have NO Donner Lake Village number to report. Group sales: 1-800-906-2871 / (530) 587-6081.
findings.price_usd: Donner Lake Inn ~$206-$214/night (off-season date query, aggregator). Donner Lake Village: no rate obtainable.
findings.restrictions: Donner Lake Inn has only 5 rooms - a party of 6 needs 3 rooms, effectively a partial buyout. Donner Lake Village splits winter rates into Holiday and non-Holiday tiers (Nov 1 - Apr 30) but publishes neither without dates.
findings.season_confirmed: NONE for winter 2026-27; the Donner Lake Inn figure is from a September date query

findings.name: Norden/Donner Summit has essentially no motel inventory - this constrains the whole trip shape
findings.claim: STRUCTURAL NEGATIVE worth stating plainly on the site. There is no conventional motel on Donner Summit. The lodging that exists at the top of the pass is: the Hotel at Sugar Bowl and its village property rentals (rates above), Clair Tappaan Lodge (hostel-style, no published rate), Rainbow Lodge down at Soda Springs (no published rate), and private vacation rentals in Serene Lakes/Soda Springs handled by local agencies. The nearest motel-grade inventory is 10-15 miles downhill in Truckee, or further west down I-80 at Cisco Grove / Emigrant Gap / Colfax, where a local directory lists options like Cisco Grove Campground & RV Park with a standard room at $80 and Sierra Woods Lodge in Emigrant Gap - but that directory carries no date and warns its information may be out of date, so those are not reportable prices. Practical consequence: a group optimising for the cheap Donner Summit lifts (Boreal, Soda Springs, Donner Ski Ranch) will almost certainly sleep in Truckee and drive up daily, which is ~15-25 miles each way and is exactly the in-area mileage the fuel estimate above accounts for.
findings.restrictions: n/a
findings.season_confirmed: NONE - structural observation, not a price
